project.name: dayspark
project.description: 开源、自托管优先的日历与待办应用（对标 Todo清单 的执行向体验）。Flutter 全平台运行，数据同步与 AI 接口由你自己的服务器掌控。

baseline_coverage.reason: AI or MCP tooling alone does not show that the project develops an agent product. The catalog applies when a project is intentionally developing agent behavior and needs behavioral acceptance cases.
Multiple project-owned assets provide evidence relevant to the catalog purpose, 'Assess a proposed change for correctness, clarity, and maintainability before acceptance.'; paths are listed below.

No sufficiently specific evidence for catalog signals: An observed failure, reproducible input, or discrepancy is available.. Applicable when a concrete failure or discrepancy needs a bounded investigation.
Multiple project-owned assets provide evidence relevant to the catalog purpose, 'Organize explanations, reference material, tutorials, and task guidance around reader needs.'; paths are listed below.

Multiple project-owned assets provide evidence relevant to the catalog purpose, 'Keep development changes traceable and reviewable through explicit version-control practices.'; paths are listed below.

Multiple project-owned assets provide evidence relevant to the catalog purpose, 'Make goals, scope, acceptance conditions, and work dependencies explicit before implementation.'; paths are listed below.

No sufficiently specific evidence for catalog signals: Claims depend on experiments, datasets, or reproducible methods.. Applicable when an investigation or experiment must report provenance, outcomes, and limitations.
Multiple project-owned assets provide evidence relevant to the catalog purpose, 'Check observable behavior with focused, repeatable tests appropriate to the change.'; paths are listed below.

evidence.claim: Requires SPEC-first changes, preservation of protected data and Git history, and full analyze/test gates before commit.
Defines traceable change rules, root-cause-first fixes, evidence-based validation, and platform-aware implementation.
Defines task briefs, implementation reports, review diffs, independent review, bounded fix cycles, and delivery rulings for multi-task work.

semantic_coverage.reason: Current governing instructions and the execution process provide a coherent, traceable and reviewable change workflow. The historical plans are not needed to establish this coverage.

evidence.claim: Requires dart analyze and the complete Flutter test suite as evidence before commits.
Requires defect reproduction, a regression test that fails before the fix, successful rerun, relevant validation and explicit completion criteria.
Runs the project's automated CI validation on repository changes.

semantic_coverage.reason: The active policy combines repeatable tests, regression evidence, change validation and CI gates; its purpose is substantively covered.

evidence.claim: Requires specification and quality verdicts, reproducible findings, evidence references and reviewers to rerun gates.
Provides an active adversarial review checklist with severity levels and concrete defect categories.
Separates a formal reviewer from the implementer and binds decisions to the exact current PR head and frozen scope.

semantic_coverage.reason: The repository has both project-level adversarial review guidance and an exact-head formal reviewer contract, with acceptance kept separate from implementation.

evidence.claim: Assigns distinct authority and audiences to SPEC, CLAUDE, CONSTRAINTS, ROADMAP, START_HERE and process documentation.
Provides a current continuation entry and directs readers to the live project state and next work.
Acts as the current project status and roadmap source.
Defines the product contracts and core behavior as the business source of truth.

semantic_coverage.reason: The active documentation set has explicit reader roles, authoritative sources, current status and stable product reference. Historical documents are distinguished by path and are not counted as current authority.

evidence.claim: Defines product scope, behavioral contracts, phased work and out-of-scope items.
Tracks current phases, status and pending work.
For multi-task work, requires briefs with acceptance criteria and dependency/interface review before implementation.

semantic_coverage.reason: The active specification, roadmap and execution process cover scope, acceptance and dependencies at a depth suited to the project; they do not require ceremony for every small edit.

evidence.claim: Requires identifying a failure's root cause before changing code and validating the correction with evidence.
Uses reproduced failures and regression tests to distinguish an observed defect from an unverified fix.
Records concrete incident symptoms, root-cause chains, fixes and verification for selected technical incidents.

semantic_coverage.reason: Root-cause-first diagnosis, reproduction and incident records are present, but the inspected active guidance does not define a general bounded debugging process for collecting execution evidence across failures. This is partial coverage, not a missing capability.

evidence.claim: Defines a calendar and task product with synchronization and an AI/MCP interface; it does not establish research experiments or dataset-based claims as a project need.
Describes product development and pending project work rather than a research or experiment workflow.

semantic_coverage.reason: The catalog's applicability condition—investigations or experiments that must report provenance, outcomes and limitations—is not established for this product. Absence of a research keyword is not treated as a gap.

evidence.claim: Describes a user-facing AI assistant using a user-supplied model key, so the repository develops AI-assisted product behavior in addition to coding-tool instructions.
Defines MCP operations and a stdio wrapper for a local Agent, including action constraints and protocol behavior.
Provides concrete MCP feature QA evidence, but does not by itself define task-level behavioral acceptance cases for the AI assistant or an agent system.

semantic_coverage.reason: The project does develop AI-assisted behavior and an agent-facing tool surface, so applicability is established. The inspected material specifies tool contracts and feature QA, but does not show a systematic set of behavioral acceptance cases for the assistant/agent behavior; MCP presence alone is insufficient for satisfied.
